_comment: Tier-2 for skfem stokes#3, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. The entry was marked inherited/unverified and said the equal-order tet pair 'produces a pressure GridFunction whose mode pattern alternates by element (checkerboard); the Functional integral of div(u) over the mesh is O(1) instead of O(eps)'. Ran: a namespace probe; the tet element inventory; a real 3D block solve; the nullity of the condensed block for Taylor-Hood ElementVector(TetP2)/TetP1 and equal-order ElementVector(TetP1)/TetP1 on MeshTet().refined(1,2,3); and a lightly regularised solve at refined(2) and (3). Printed: GridFunction IS NGSOLVE VOCABULARY -- hasattr(skfem,'GridFunction') is False and no name in the skfem namespace contains it; a skfem Stokes solution is a plain 1-D numpy.ndarray of the stacked [u; p] vector whose pressure is a slice at offset basis_u.N (345 here, 26 pressure DOFs). ElementTetP2 and ElementTetP1 both exist, so the recommendation itself is sound. THE INF-SUP FAILURE IS COUNTABLE WITHOUT SOLVING: the spurious-mode count is CONSTANT at 4/4/4 for Taylor-Hood across three refinements while equal-order grows 25/63/71 -- a sharper, mesh-independent statement of 'checkerboard'. A regularised solve agrees: the Taylor-Hood pressure range is 7.6249e-01 then 7.9203e-01 (bounded, converging) while equal order goes 1.2543e+00 to 2.8429e+01. NOT REPRODUCED and therefore not asserted: the entry's 'integral of div(u) is O(1) instead of O(eps)' -- under a regularised solve the relative divergence of the two pairs is comparable and does not separate them.
